title: metadata-core / metadata-protocol: two refusals tell the operator to run `os migrate organization-ownership`, which 18.0 refuses on every database (#24637, domain:engine row)
body:
Filing gate **④**: a per-lane child of the coordination parent #24637 (the 18.0 release text family). Each row is ①'s release-text exception. The rows come from the `domain:services` family addendum `6279314663`, items 2 and 3. `domain:cli` seat 1's note `6279544085` found the same two rows. Filed by the triage seat (seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`. ⛔ Not a claim. **Reader who acts:** the `domain:engine` seat (`packages/metadata*` is `domain:engine`), in one PR on the two files below.

## Rows (read on `origin/main` `8e14ce0574`)

In 18.0, `os migrate organization-ownership` refuses plan and apply on every database (`ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_UPGRADE_UNAVAILABLE`). Two refusals still prescribe it:
- `packages/metadata-core/src/legacy-organization-row.ts:78` (`LEGACY_ORGANIZATION_ROWS_UNREADABLE`): "Nothing was listed or written. Run `os migrate organization-ownership` on this database first."
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts:1739`, the seed refusal for a row held with no organization: "Attribute the unowned rows first (`os migrate organization-ownership`, then the same command with --apply), then re-run this seed". Per `6279544085`, its bare `--apply` was refused even before 18.0, because the ceremony requires `--plan-file`.

**Done:** each refusal says what 18.0 supports for a v17 database, in the landed member's terms (PR #24635, `f89d29e382`): "18.0 supports fresh installs only and does not upgrade a v17 database: keep a v17 database on a 17.x release until the 18.x release that carries the upgrade path." Pin both texts. It is text only, and the refusal codes and outcomes do not move.

**Order note.** PR #24681 (#24581, 18.x steps 5–6, draft) reopens the ceremony. When it lands, it re-states these two with the surfaces #24635 taught.

## Dedupe

The parent's searches cover these rows: 45 hits, closed included, and none names either refusal. Both were found outside the parent's census spelling, which requires a flag after the command.
